label: second copy step (recall_idx 1), boosted when orig(1)/orig(2) are j/k/v/a
explanation: Fires only at the second copy step (t = L+1, recall_idx 1: input is orig(0) fed back after <DEL>, output is orig(1)). It never fires on any other step: original phase, delimiter, or later copy steps. Within that step it is on for about 16% of sequences, and which ones depends on the content of the upcoming outputs. It is much more likely, and stronger, when the token being output (orig(1)) or the next one (orig(2)) is j, k, v or a (j has 8x lift, k 7x, v 6x, a 5x; y and t are weaker). The top activations all have j/k at orig(1..3), e.g. h j j 1 k o. It is more frequent at L = 5..7. The input token itself barely matters. recall_idx==1 alone gives recall 1.0 but precision 0.16; the j/k/v/a condition raises F1 to about 0.56 and mass recall to about 0.83. The remaining selectivity looks like a graded weighting over the upcoming tokens that a boolean predicate does not capture cleanly.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: j, k, v, a, y, t; least: q, x, f, 0) and the next token to output (most: j, k, v, 1, a, t; least: g, b, q, 0); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=6 & t=7, L=7 & t=8.
